entries.appliesTo: New York state agencies, state and local authorities, and political subdivisions (technology procurement)

sources.procurementRules: SFL § 163-e(1)(a) — 'the state and any department, bureau, board, commission, authority, and any other agency or instrumentality of the state shall not enter into or renew any contract or agreement to procure technology, including hardware, systems, devices, software, or services that include embedded or incidental information technology, which are prohibited from federal procurement pursuant to section 889 of Public Law 115-232 of 2018'; GML § 103-h(1)(a) — 'a political subdivision shall not enter into or renew any contract or agreement to procure technology'
sources.program: SFL § 163-e(2) — 'The office of information technology services shall, in consultation with the division of homeland security and emergency services and the office of general services, establish and update regularly a list of restricted technology. Technology on this list shall not be procured by any state agency, state or local authority, or political subdivision'

flags: substitution: NY S 8793 was replaced by A 9456 (legiscan.js relation 'replaced by: A 9456'); coded from the A 9456 text (texts/ny-a-9456.txt) under this id per instruction — A 9456 is not separately in the dataset, so this is not marked duplicate

AI relevance is indirect: the bill amends a 2025 chapter (S. 3259/A. 2237) on security-threat technology procurement; the amendment strikes the prior definition of 'information and communications technology' — which had expressly excluded 'automated-decision making systems' — and substitutes 'technology' as defined in SFL § 160(10), a definition not restated in this text

waiver-notice requirement fits no listed duty: any agency or political subdivision obtaining a federal § 889 waiver 'must provide notice of any such waiver granted to the office of information technology services within thirty days of waiver approval' (SFL § 163-e(3)(d); GML § 103-h(2)(d))

waiver pathway: OITS with named agencies 'may provide a waiver from this section' on findings of state interest, no compliant product at non-prohibitive price, and no network-security compromise (SFL § 163-e(3); GML § 103-h(2))

UAV exemption: unmanned aerial vehicles are exempt from the restriction if collected data 'is stored and maintained exclusively within the United States' and 'is not accessible to the business or entity that would otherwise be subject to restriction' or the UAV 'is operated using software developed and maintained in the United States' (SFL § 163-e(4))

duty on OITS itself (not the procuring agencies): 'shall issue guidance to all state agencies and local procurement authorities necessary, including providing updates on prohibited or excluded entities for procurement contracts in conformity with federal law, rules and regulations, no later than sixty days after any entity is prohibited or excluded' (§ 3 of the amended 2025 chapter)
grandfathering: nothing requires pre-effective-date resident technology 'to be removed or replaced' (SFL § 163-e(5); GML § 103-h(3))
no penalty or enforcement provision in the text — exposure omitted
